prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which heterobifunctional molecules bring a chosen protein and a ubiquitin ligase together so that the protein is removed

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B029 plus B052 to B007 alone, and I want to give the scientific reason and not the support count. My round-1 objection was evidentiary: I ranked B007 fourth because I doubted that the claim rested on determined structures. Reading the first round again, the Ciulli strand answers that. The VHL ligand chemistry was built from crystal structures of the ligase with its substrate peptide, and the ternary-complex structures with a degrader bound to both partners explain cooperativity and linker selectivity in atomic terms. That is the kind of evidence I ask for: the mechanism was seen, not inferred, and the design rules were then confirmed by many independent groups across several E3 ligases. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and the first demonstration in 2001, so the three names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli divide the credit cleanly into idea, proof of concept and structure-guided chemistry. It is also a new modality and not another bond class, which answers the chair's question about conceptual step better than B029 does.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet an approved drug, so the medical consequence is projected, and I still hold that a principle-based prize should not be awarded on promise alone; I accept B007 only because the chemical principle is independently confirmed in structures and kinetics. The 2001 PROTAC was peptidic and cell-impermeable, so the decisive drug-like chemistry came later, and the committee must be sure the citation does not credit a refinement as a discovery. The cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto) is a separate mechanism with real claims, and a three-name prize leaves it out; the citation must say heterobifunctional degraders and not claim all of degradation. Finally, moving to a single part gives up the second achievement I had proposed, and B029 and B052 remain mature, cleanly attributed cases that I would be content to see awarded.

responses.point: B029 extends the 2010 prize to another bond class, so the conceptual step is smaller than a new organising principle, and B001 should rank above it on originality.
responses.response: This is the fair objection and I now accept most of it. Amine binding, deprotonation and avoidance of beta-hydride elimination make C-N coupling mechanistically distinct, but it is still a new bond class built on a mechanism the 2010 prize already honoured, so I no longer put it first. On B001 we still differ. My doubt is the one I gave in round 1: evidence for equilibrium phase separation at endogenous concentrations in vivo is not yet at the level of a determined structure or a measured binding constant, and Pappu and Mittag are left out of your trio. I would be convinced by quantitative phase diagrams in cells at native expression and by perturbations that separate function from aggregation, and I do not think the field has them yet.

responses.point: B029 is overdue and not premature, a clean two-person prize with a mechanism understood and industrial use that can be checked in the literature.
responses.response: I agree with your attribution, Buchwald and Hartwig without Kosugi, and with maturity, and I answered the chair's question the way you did, by pointing to amine binding and base-mediated deprotonation as the new steps. Where I have changed is the comparison. After the first round I think the step is real but smaller than a new modality, and B007 has structural evidence that C-N coupling does not need to provide. I would not oppose B029 and I keep it as my first alternative. My view of B028 is unchanged: seven claimants still make it hard to cut to three.

responses.point: Ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design and structure-guided VHL ligands are measured quantitatively, and degraders already reach late-stage trials, though the cereblon and PROTAC strands are partly separate.
responses.response: Your quantitative argument is what moved me, because I can check it against the structures. I share your caution about the glue strand: if the citation says only degradation, the omission of Handa and Ito will be hard to defend, so I propose wording around heterobifunctional degraders and the ligase recruitment principle. You asked in round 1 for clinical status to be verified in the expert report, and I support that; I would not make approval a condition, but I would want the report to say which degraders are in phase 3.

responses.point: B007 is a coherent three-person prize explained in one sentence, but the first PROTAC paper was a proof of concept with peptidic molecules, so the decisive drug-like chemistry may be later.
responses.response: Your point about 2001 is the one that matters for the citation. Crews and Deshaies established that a bifunctional molecule can direct a ligase to a new substrate, and Ciulli's VHL ligand work and ternary structures turned that into a design rule. I think the two are each essential and not refinements, since without the structural account of cooperativity the concept would not have become rational chemistry. I would therefore keep the trio and avoid wording that credits drug approval. On your question for round 2 about a single coherent achievement against a two-part prize, I now prefer the single part: pairing synthesis with genome editing, as I proposed, made a diluted citation.

responses.point: B007 is mechanistically precise and independently confirmed, but the cut between PROTACs and cereblon glues is an attribution risk and expert-report evaluation should confirm that 2001 and the later ligand chemistry are each essential.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution risk is the main residual one and that the expert report should settle it. My reading is that the three-name PROTAC slate is defensible because the glue strand is a different mechanism, found by phenotype and target identification and not by design, so it can be treated as its own future prize. On B052 I note your Target-AID point about Nishida and Kondo, which I raised too, and I would not hold a Liu-only prize hostage to it, but that is why I keep B052 only as an alternative.

responses.point: B052 and B007 are two distinct achievements that turn a biological process into a defined chemical reaction, but two prizes in one year risk a diluted citation and the three-person cap forces a cut.
responses.response: I think your pairing is coherent, and on B052 I still hold that deaminase editing is chemistry distinct from the 2020 cut-and-repair prize, with Liu alone as the right attribution. My difficulty is the cap. Fitting a second part beside B007 means dropping Ciulli, whose structural work is exactly what gives me confidence in the degradation case, and leaving two names that rest on the 2001 proof of concept. I would sooner award one achievement with its structural basis intact than two with a thinner one.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report confirms late-stage clinical status of degraders, and whether the committee will accept a projected clinical consequence for this prize.
Whether the committee will take Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the right three, or prefer Handa for the cereblon strand, which changes the citation.
Whether the 2001 peptidic PROTAC is judged a discovery or a proof of concept that later chemistry made real.
Whether colleagues who prefer a cleaner molecule-making achievement will see B029 or a Liu-only B052 as stronger than a modality whose drugs are not yet approved.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I have no known personal or institutional connection to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli or any other shortlisted candidate. My Stockholm University colleague relationship with Secretary Peter Brzezinski is not relevant to any candidate. My structural-chemistry background inclines me toward cases supported by determined structures, which I disclose as a disciplinary lean.
